findings.message: counts[p.Name]++ is executed outside the mutex (after mu.Unlock()) while other goroutines may concurrently read/write the same counts map. Concurrent writes to a Go map can panic with 'concurrent map writes' or silently corrupt counts, making the n != 1 validation unreliable and Collect nondeterministic.
findings.suggestion: Move the increment inside the mutex (e.g. mu.Lock(); out[p.Name] = ms; counts[p.Name]++; mu.Unlock()) or use a per-index slice/atomic counters like errs instead of a shared map.

findings.message: Describe() still builds a names slice (and appends every probe name) only to use len(names); since len(names) == len(c.probes), the loop and allocation are unnecessary work on every call.
findings.suggestion: Return fmt.Sprintf("%d probes registered", len(c.probes)) directly and drop the names slice/loop (or keep it only if probe names are needed elsewhere).
